overall: The AG found the Andover School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in its June 8 litigation-strategy executive session or its notice, and declined to review two allegations not first raised with the committee.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee entered executive session on June 8 for an improper purpose, since no one had threatened litigation over records requests.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussion in executive session was proper under Purpose 3 where it pertained to a decision to pursue litigation against an individual.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the June 8 meeting notice was insufficiently detailed because it did not identify the litigation matter to be discussed in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Because identifying the litigation matter or the individual could have had a detrimental effect on the Committee's litigating position, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting certain information regarding the anticipated executive session on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to discuss his Open Meeting Law complaint during a meeting; this was not first raised with the committee.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these allegations because they were not included in a complaint to the Committee and the Committee has not had an opportunity to respond.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee deliberated outside a properly posted meeting; this was not first raised with the committee.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these allegations because they were not included in a complaint to the Committee and the Committee has not had an opportunity to respond.
